methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atoms is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $1.7B to date. The valuation analysis relies on a comp universe of nine peers across Robotics & Manufacturing—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics—though same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables proved insufficient for a traditional peer-median approach.

Given the sparse near-peer dataset, Stage-Progression methodology was the primary applicable triangulation technique. Using the $1.7B total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage progression, the method implies a valuation of $2.0B. This represents the central point in the derived range, with low and high anchors at $1.7B and $2.3B respectively, the latter reflecting upside sensitivity around stage-transition assumptions.

The $1.7B–$2.3B range, centered on $2.0B, reflects the constraint of a single primary methodology. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient narrow-peer data to validate via multiples-based approaches and reliance on stage-progression step-up factors that may not capture sector-specific growth dynamics or this founder's prior exit history. Additional private-market transaction data or public-market comps in robotics would materially improve conviction in this valuation band.
